steps.intent: Our objective is to secure a clean one-year renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, retaining targeted measures to support the Algiers Agreement, accountability, and the safe MINUSMA drawdown. We have kept the text focused on existing criteria and humanitarian safeguards so it can attract broad support, while flagging concern at abuses by all actors, including foreign private military personnel. Difficult points will be Mali’s request to lift sanctions and any attempt by some members to weaken human-rights reporting or remove references to foreign security personnel; we expect Russia and China to seek amendments. We will resist dilution of the Panel’s reporting and the sanctions list while remaining open to technical language to avoid a veto.

messages.Albania: Albania supports renewing the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate. We ask the penholder to strengthen the text by explicitly naming the Wagner Group in PP8 and OP3 and by adding a clear operative call for IHL and human rights compliance and accountability by all forces, including foreign private military personnel. We must preserve the Panel's existing human rights and IHL reporting and access.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, given the continuing grave security and human rights situation. We ask the penholder to reflect continued support for Algeria’s leadership in the mediation process, consistent with resolution 2690, and to add an explicit call for safe and unhindered humanitarian access. Brazil can support the text with these adjustments.
messages.China: China supports renewing the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate. We welcome the text's reaffirmation of Mali's sovereignty and primary responsibility, its humanitarian exemptions and its reference to resolution 2664. We expect the Panel to cooperate closely with the Transition Government of Mali and for all measures to remain targeted and avoid adverse humanitarian effects. China will vote in favour.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports renewing the targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate. We ask that OP7 explicitly mandate the Panel to monitor and report on unintended humanitarian impact, and that OP8 include accountability for violations and abuses by all actors, including foreign private military and security personnel. With these refinements, Ecuador can support the draft.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports renewing the sanctions regime as a temporary tool to support peace, but the text should respond more directly to Mali's request and to African concerns. We propose a mid-term review with a clear path to suspension or lifting, and ask that the Panel report on the humanitarian impact of the measures. These changes would help preserve consensus and reaffirm Mali's sovereignty.
messages.Ghana: Ghana supports the renewal of the Mali sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate, which remain important for accountability and peace. We ask the penholder to strengthen the text by adding climate-security language, an operative reference to continued AU/ECOWAS engagement, and a clearer review clause that allows the Council to adjust or lift measures in light of progress. These changes reflect the A3’s emphasis that the international community’s engagement with Mali must continue beyond MINUSMA’s withdrawal.
messages.Japan: Japan supports renewing the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, and thanks France and the United Arab Emirates for the balanced text. We would like the text to reflect Japan's emphasis on the orderly withdrawal of MINUSMA and the transfer of its tasks, and to state clearly that all security operations, including those conducted with foreign security personnel, must comply with international humanitarian and human rights law. These points are important for accountability and protection of civilians; Japan can support the draft with these adjustments.
messages.Malta: Malta supports renewal of the 2374 sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate. We would like the text to make explicit, in OP6, the obligation to respect the Status of Forces Agreement and freedom of movement during MINUSMA's drawdown and withdrawal, and, in OP8, to include protection of civilians, safe and unhindered humanitarian access and women's full, equal and meaningful participation in the political transition.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the draft as it stands. It is balanced, renews targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts, and reaffirms Mali's sovereignty, the Algiers Agreement and the transition timeline. We welcome the humanitarian exemptions and the review clause, and encourage full cooperation with the Panel of Experts.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support a renewal of the Mali sanctions regime. The Transition Government has clearly requested that these measures be lifted, and the Council should respect that sovereign decision rather than maintain intrusive human rights and expert-reporting mechanisms that single out Mali and its partners. We therefore call for the draft to be reworked to let the measures expire on 31 August 2023 and to remove references to foreign private military and security personnel.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland supports the renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, and we welcome the text’s focus on accountability, human rights and humanitarian exemptions. We ask the penholder to add a reference to fair and clear procedures for listings and delistings, and to include international humanitarian law explicitly in the OP8 progress review. We can support the text with these adjustments.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates supports the draft as presented and is pleased to co-sponsor it. We welcome the reaffirmation of humanitarian exemptions, including resolution 2664 (2022), and the emphasis on accountability and protection of civilians. We encourage the Council to maintain a unified position as MINUSMA draws down and to keep the sanctions measures under review.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom supports renewal of the 2374 sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate; a gap would undermine accountability and the Algiers process. We would like the text to name the Wagner Group where it refers to foreign private military and security personnel, and to make explicit that the Panel reports on conflict-related sexual violence and obstruction of MINUSMA’s drawdown. We also seek clearer language on unhindered, timely and safe access for the Panel, including from the Transition Government, and on keeping sanctions under review in light of cooperation with the Panel and MINUSMA’s withdrawal.
messages.United States of America: The United States supports renewing the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate. We ask the penholder to explicitly name the Wagner Group and to ensure the Panel reports on Wagner and other foreign private military and security personnel, including attacks on United Nations personnel and obstruction of MINUSMA’s drawdown and withdrawal. With those strengthening changes, we can support the text.

It avoids explicitly naming the Wagner Group as a compromise to avert a Russian veto, though several Western asks are only partially met. Expected adoption is 14-0-1, with Russia abstaining.

messages.Albania: Albania supports the current text as a consensus renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate. We would have preferred an explicit reference to the Wagner Group, but we recognize that the language on foreign private military and security personnel, together with the strengthened accountability and reporting provisions, captures our core concerns. We urge full implementation of the resolution and call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with MINUSMA’s drawdown and respect the Status of Forces Agreement.
messages.Brazil: Brazil supports the revised draft and welcomes that our previous concerns on Algeria-led mediation and humanitarian access have been reflected. We value the targeted nature of the sanctions, the humanitarian safeguards and exemptions, and the review clause that takes account of Mali’s request and progress on the Agreement and human rights. Brazil therefore does not request further changes and is ready to vote in favour.
messages.China: China supports the current draft and will vote in favour. We welcome the retention of humanitarian exemptions and the reference to Mali’s request, and we stress that the sanctions regime must be implemented with full respect for Mali’s sovereignty and Government ownership. We call for close coordination with the Transition Government to ensure MINUSMA’s safe and orderly withdrawal and the Panel of Experts’ cooperative engagement.
messages.Ecuador: Ecuador supports the draft as revised. We welcome the inclusion of monitoring of unintended humanitarian impact and accountability for violations by all actors, including foreign private military and security personnel. We encourage the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the Panel of Experts and to respect the Status of Forces Agreement during MINUSMA’s withdrawal. Ecuador is ready to support adoption of the text.
messages.Gabon: Gabon supports the revised text as it stands. We welcome the inclusion of the 29 February 2024 review, the humanitarian-impact reporting and the list review, which respond to our concerns and to Mali’s request. We encourage the Council to keep the sanctions under close review with a view to suspension or lifting as progress is made, and we call for full cooperation with the Panel of Experts and a safe MINUSMA drawdown and withdrawal.
messages.Ghana: Ghana welcomes the inclusion of our priorities on climate-security, regional engagement, and a sanctions review with a view to adjustment or lifting in light of progress. We support the current text and call for its adoption. Ghana urges the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the United Nations and the Panel of Experts, respect the Status of Forces Agreement during MINUSMA’s withdrawal, and ensure accountability and protection of civilians.
messages.Japan: Japan supports the current text and welcomes the inclusion of the compliance paragraph and the reference to the smooth and proper transfer of MINUSMA’s tasks. We call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the United Nations and the Panel of Experts, respect the Status of Forces Agreement, and ensure accountability and humanitarian access. Japan remains committed to the Agreement, the political transition and the protection of civilians.
messages.Malta: Malta thanks France and the co-sponsors for the revised text and welcomes the incorporation of its previous requests on the Status of Forces Agreement, freedom of movement, protection of civilians, humanitarian access and the full, equal and meaningful participation of women. Malta supports the current draft and calls for its swift adoption, with continued emphasis on a safe and orderly MINUSMA withdrawal, accountability for violations, and regular review of the sanctions measures.
messages.Mozambique: Mozambique supports the revised text as a balanced renewal that keeps the sanctions targeted, preserves humanitarian exemptions, and acknowledges Mali's request for review. We welcome the references to the African Union and ECOWAS, the safe withdrawal of MINUSMA, and the importance of accountability. We have no further changes and are ready to vote in favour.
messages.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation cannot support a draft that renews the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts against the clearly expressed request of the host Government. Our red lines remain: the sanctions measures must expire on 31 August 2023, and all references to foreign private military and security personnel and intrusive human rights conditionality must be removed. If these changes are not made, we will not be in a position to support the text.
messages.Switzerland: Switzerland thanks the penholder for incorporating our requests on fair and clear sanctions procedures, IHL in the review, and reporting on humanitarian impact. We support the current text as a balanced renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts mandate, with a clear review and delisting process. We underline the importance of full compliance with IHL and international human rights law by all actors, including foreign private military and security personnel, and of safe, unhindered humanitarian access and protection of civilians during and after MINUSMA’s withdrawal.
messages.United Arab Emirates: The United Arab Emirates supports the current text and retains its co-sponsorship. We welcome the balanced renewal of the sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate, including the clear humanitarian exemptions, the review clause taking into account Mali’s request, and the emphasis on accountability and safe MINUSMA withdrawal. We encourage the Council to maintain a unified position and adopt the draft as it stands.
messages.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom thanks France and the United Arab Emirates and welcomes the inclusion of conflict-related sexual violence, obstruction of MINUSMA’s drawdown, and strengthened access provisions. We continue to believe the Council must be explicit about the Wagner Group’s role; generic references to foreign private military and security personnel do not adequately capture the documented risks. We therefore ask that the Wagner Group be named in PP8 and OP9. This is not a red line, but it is important for the credibility of the text.
messages.United States of America: The United States thanks France for its engagement and for incorporating strengthened reporting on foreign private military and security personnel, including obstruction of MINUSMA’s drawdown and attacks against United Nations personnel. While we would have preferred explicit naming of the Wagner Group, we recognize the compromise reflected in the text and believe it preserves the essential reporting and accountability tools. We support the current draft and urge its swift adoption.

replies.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: rejected: explicit naming of Wagner not added to preserve consensus and avoid a veto; generic language retained.

reasons.Albania: Albania has consistently supported the Mali sanctions mandate and MINUSMA’s orderly withdrawal while stressing human rights, accountability and concerns about the Wagner Group. The draft is a balanced renewal with review and humanitarian safeguards, so Albania would vote in favour.
reasons.Brazil: Brazil had already indicated support and requested no changes; the draft reflects its priorities on targeted sanctions, humanitarian safeguards, sovereignty and review. Voting in favour is consistent with Brazil’s earlier support for renewing the Mali sanctions and Panel of Experts.
reasons.China: China had already indicated support and made no requests for changes; the draft is consistent with its support for renewed sanctions and the Panel of Experts while preserving Malian sovereignty and a review of measures.
reasons.Ecuador: Ecuador supported the draft in the last negotiation round and its provisions align with Ecuador’s support for UN sanctions, accountability, humanitarian safeguards and a review of measures in light of Mali’s request. Ecuador would therefore vote in favour.
reasons.France: France is the penholder and co-sponsor of the draft, so it strongly supports renewing the Mali sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate while keeping the review mechanism in light of Mali’s request. Voting in favour and explaining the vote before the vote is consistent with France’s stated policy on accountability, MINUSMA withdrawal, and targeted sanctions.
reasons.Gabon: Gabon has consistently supported renewals of the Mali sanctions regime and had already indicated support for this draft. The text includes a review clause and humanitarian safeguards consistent with Gabon’s concerns, so no pre-vote explanation was necessary.
reasons.Ghana: Ghana supported the draft in the last negotiation round, has consistently backed a balanced Mali sanctions/accountability framework, and welcomes the review and humanitarian safeguards. A yes vote with an explanation reinforces Ghana’s A3, sovereignty, accountability and humanitarian priorities.
reasons.Japan: Japan supports renewing the Mali sanctions and Panel of Experts mandate, with strong emphasis on human rights, humanitarian safeguards, and MINUSMA withdrawal cooperation; its national policy and prior Council record favour voting in favour.
reasons.Malta: Malta had already signalled support and no changes; voting in favour is consistent with its focus on accountability, protection of civilians, humanitarian access, and safe MINUSMA withdrawal. The draft renews targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate, matching Malta’s established position on this file.
reasons.Mozambique: Mozambique supported the prior consensus on Mali, requested no changes, and the draft maintains targeted sanctions with humanitarian safeguards and a review clause, consistent with its support for peace, stability and African-led mediation.
reasons.Russian Federation: The draft retains the sanctions regime and Panel of Experts despite Mali’s request to lift them and rejects Russia’s red lines, so Russia exercises its veto to protect Bamako and oppose Western pressure.
reasons.Switzerland: Switzerland supports targeted sanctions, accountability and humanitarian safeguards; the draft contains regular review, delisting provisions, and humanitarian exemptions consistent with Swiss policy. It therefore votes in favour.
reasons.United Arab Emirates: The UAE is a co-sponsor and recorded support with no requested changes, so it votes in favour. Its statement emphasizes sovereignty, humanitarian safeguards, accountability and orderly MINUSMA withdrawal, consistent with its prior support for resolutions 2640, 2649 and 2690.
reasons.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The UK supports renewing sanctions and the Panel of Experts and has consistently backed consensus on Mali while expressing concerns about Wagner and human rights. Despite rejected amendments, a yes vote aligns with UK policy and avoids undermining the resolution.
reasons.United States of America: The draft renews targeted sanctions and the Panel of Experts mandate, consistent with U.S. policy to press accountability, constrain Wagner-linked abuses, and support Mali’s transition while preserving humanitarian safeguards. The United States therefore votes yes and explains its support before the vote.

before.Albania: Albania will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts. These measures are not intended to harm the civilian population, and the humanitarian safeguards and review provisions are important. We note the request of the Transition Government of Mali to lift the sanctions, but sanctions remain necessary to support accountability, the implementation of the Algiers Agreement and compliance with international humanitarian law and human rights law. We call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with MINUSMA’s drawdown and withdrawal, respect the Status of Forces Agreement, and ensure that all security operations, including those involving foreign private military personnel, comply with international law. We support the proposed review with a view to adjusting or lifting measures in light of concrete progress.
before.Brazil: Brazil will vote in favour of the draft resolution. We support the renewal of the sanctions measures and the Panel of Experts, which remain important tools to support peace, accountability and the implementation of the Algiers Agreement in Mali. At the same time, we stress that sanctions must be targeted and subject to fair and clear procedures, with full respect for humanitarian exemptions and without adverse consequences for the civilian population. Brazil reaffirms its commitment to Mali’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, and calls for full respect for human rights and international humanitarian law by all actors, accountability for violations, unhindered humanitarian access, and progress toward the agreed political transition. We also welcome the provision to keep the measures under review with a view to adjusting or lifting them in light of progress.
before.Ecuador: Ecuador will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts as tools to promote accountability, protect civilians and support the implementation of the Algiers Agreement. We take note of the request of the Transition Government of Mali and welcome the provisions for review and delisting. We call on the Malian authorities to cooperate fully with the United Nations during MINUSMA’s withdrawal, to respect the Status of Forces Agreement, and to ensure that all security operations comply with international human rights law and international humanitarian law. We also welcome the reaffirmation that these measures are not intended to have adverse humanitarian consequences for the civilian population.
before.France: France thanks all Council members for the constructive negotiations on this important text. We vote in favour of this resolution, which renews the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts at a critical moment for Mali and the region. These measures are not an end in themselves; they are tools to support the implementation of the Algiers Agreement, to combat impunity, to protect civilians and to constrain those who obstruct peace and reconciliation. France has listened carefully to the request of the Transition Government of Mali, and the text therefore provides for a review by 29 February 2024 and for consideration of appropriate adjustments, including suspension or lifting, in light of concrete progress. We stress that sanctions are targeted and are not intended to have adverse humanitarian consequences for the civilian population. France also underscores the need for full accountability for violations of international human rights law and international humanitarian law committed by all actors, including foreign private military and security personnel. We call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the United Nations, including the Panel of Experts, and to ensure the safe, orderly and timely withdrawal and liquidation of MINUSMA, in full respect of the Status of Forces Agreement. France urges all members to support this balanced and necessary text.
before.Ghana: Ghana votes in favour of this draft resolution. We align ourselves with the position of the A3 and welcome the balanced renewal of the sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, including the provisions on humanitarian exemptions and the scheduled review. We stress that the sanctions regime must continue to support peace and accountability in Mali, including for violations of international human rights law and international humanitarian law and obstruction of the Algiers Agreement. Ghana reiterates its respect for Mali’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity, and calls on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the Panel of Experts and with the orderly and safe withdrawal and liquidation of MINUSMA, including full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement, protection of civilians, accountability, and unhindered humanitarian access. We also underscore that the sanctions measures should remain under review in light of progress, including the request of the Malian authorities, with a view to their appropriate adjustment, suspension or lifting as conditions warrant.
before.Japan: Japan will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of the sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, including its reporting on human rights and international humanitarian law violations, obstruction of the Algiers Agreement, support to armed groups, and obstruction of MINUSMA’s drawdown and withdrawal. At the same time, Japan stresses that sanctions must not have adverse humanitarian consequences for the civilian population, and we welcome the humanitarian exemptions and the provisions for review and delisting. We call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the United Nations, respect the Status of Forces Agreement until the final departure of MINUSMA, and ensure that all security operations, including those involving foreign private military and security personnel, are conducted in full compliance with international obligations. Japan also underscores the importance of progress on the political transition, the return to constitutional order by March 2024, protection of civilians, accountability, and implementation of the Agreement on Peace and Reconciliation in Mali. We thank the penholder for its efforts.
before.Malta: Malta will vote in favour of this draft resolution. We support the renewal of targeted measures and the Panel of Experts’ mandate, which remain important tools for accountability, for the implementation of the Algiers Agreement and for supporting the safe and orderly withdrawal and liquidation of MINUSMA. We reiterate that these measures are not intended to have adverse humanitarian consequences, and we call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the United Nations, respect the Status of Forces Agreement, protect civilians and ensure accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and international human rights law.
before.Russian Federation: The Russian Federation has consistently supported the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of Mali and the right of its Government to determine the means of ensuring security and protecting the population. The sanctions regime established by resolution 2374 (2017) was conceived as temporary support to peace, but years later it has not improved the situation and is increasingly being used as a tool of external pressure on Bamako. The Transition Government of Mali has made a clear and sovereign request to lift these measures, and the Council must respect that request, especially as Mali is making serious efforts to counter terrorism and complete its political transition. Regrettably, the draft before us disregards this legitimate request. It renews the sanctions and extends the Panel of Experts, while retaining language that singles out Mali’s counter-terrorism partners and introduces new conditionality. Such provisions, including references to foreign private military and security personnel and to alleged violations by Malian forces, are unacceptable. They go beyond the Council’s mandate, rely on unverified and politicized claims, and interfere in Mali’s sovereign right to choose its partners, including in the fight against terrorism. We also note that the legitimate concerns of my delegation were not taken into account in the negotiations. For these reasons, the Russian Federation cannot support this draft. We will vote against it. We call on the Council to respect Mali’s sovereignty and to focus on practical support for counter-terrorism, humanitarian assistance and implementation of the Algiers Agreement rather than maintaining outdated sanctions. Russia will continue to provide comprehensive bilateral assistance to the people and Government of Mali.
before.Switzerland:
Mr. President,

Switzerland will vote in favour of the draft resolution before us. We support a targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts as tools to support peace, the implementation of the Algiers Agreement, and accountability in Mali. We note the request of the Transition Government of Mali to lift the sanctions measures. At this stage, however, we believe that continued review, clear benchmarks and the possibility of delisting are the right approach. We welcome that the text provides for a review by 29 February 2024, for the Committee to review designations with a view to delisting, and that it reaffirms the humanitarian exemptions, including those under resolution 2664 (2022). These elements are important for the legitimacy and humanitarian coherence of the sanctions regime.

We underline the need for full implementation of the Algiers Agreement, for the protection of civilians, and for compliance with international humanitarian law and international human rights law by all parties, including foreign private military and security personnel. We call for accountability for violations and abuses. We also call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the United Nations, including the Panel of Experts, and to respect the Status of Forces Agreement and ensure the safety and security of United Nations personnel during MINUSMA’s drawdown, withdrawal and liquidation. Switzerland remains engaged in support of the people of Mali and of a credible return to constitutional order.
before.United Arab Emirates: Mr. President, the United Arab Emirates will vote in favour of this resolution. As a co-sponsor, we support the renewal of the sanctions measures and the mandate of the Panel of Experts, which remain important tools in support of peace and stability in Mali. At the same time, we underscore that sanctions should be kept under review, with fair and clear procedures and full respect for humanitarian exemptions. We call on all parties to accelerate implementation of the Algiers Agreement, protect civilians, comply with international humanitarian law and international human rights law, and ensure accountability for violations. We also stress the importance of an orderly, safe and coordinated drawdown and withdrawal of MINUSMA, with full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement. The sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity and independence of Mali must be upheld. The UAE remains committed to working with Mali, the United Nations and regional partners in support of peace, stability and development.
before.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort: The United Kingdom will vote in favour of this resolution. We support the renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts, which remain essential for supporting peace and stability, accountability, and full implementation of the Algiers Agreement. We regret that the Council has not been able to name the Wagner Group explicitly, given the serious concerns about its activities and their impact on the Malian people. We will continue to press for accountability for human rights abuses and violations, unhindered humanitarian access, respect for the Status of Forces Agreement, and a safe and orderly MINUSMA withdrawal. We urge the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the Panel and to make concrete progress on human rights, impunity and the return to constitutional order.
before.United States of America:
The United States will vote in favour of this resolution. We thank France and the United Arab Emirates for their work to renew the Mali sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts at a critical moment for Mali, for the region, and for the Security Council’s credibility.

These are targeted measures. They are not intended to punish the Malian people, and this resolution preserves the humanitarian exemptions and carve-outs that help ensure sanctions do not impede life-saving assistance. But the Council must continue to monitor serious violations and abuses, obstruction of the Algiers Agreement, support to armed groups and terrorist organizations, and the activities of foreign private military and security personnel, including the Wagner Group. The Panel of Experts must be able to carry out that work safely and without obstruction, and the Transition Government must cooperate fully, including during MINUSMA’s drawdown, withdrawal and liquidation, in line with resolution 2690.

The United States takes note of the Transition Government’s request to lift sanctions. We believe the appropriate response is not an unconditional lifting of measures, but continued review against real progress: implementation of the peace Agreement, the fight against impunity, human rights compliance, protection of civilians, unhindered humanitarian access, and a genuine return to constitutional order by March 2024. We urge the Transition Government to make that progress and to cooperate with this Council and the Panel of Experts. The United States will continue to support the Malian people’s aspirations for peace, stability, and accountable, democratic governance.

after.Brazil:
Mr. President,

Brazil voted in favour of the draft resolution and regrets that it was not adopted, notwithstanding the broad support it received in this Council. We believe that the renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and of the mandate of the Panel of Experts was a measured and necessary contribution to peace, accountability and the implementation of the Algiers Agreement, while preserving humanitarian exemptions and providing for review and delisting.

Brazil reiterates its respect for Mali’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity and takes note of the concerns expressed by the Transition Government. It is precisely because we respect Mali and its people that we consider that the Council should retain calibrated tools to support the fight against impunity, to discourage obstruction of the peace process and to accompany the orderly withdrawal and liquidation of MINUSMA. Sanctions are not intended to punish the Malian population; they must remain targeted, subject to fair and clear procedures and fully consistent with humanitarian action.

At the same time, we call on all parties in Mali, including the Transition Government, to cooperate fully with the United Nations, to respect the Status of Forces Agreement until the final departure of MINUSMA, to protect civilians and to comply strictly with international human rights law and international humanitarian law. Accountability for violations by all actors is essential.

Brazil remains committed to constructive engagement with all Council members and with the Malian authorities, and reiterates its support for the mediation led by Algeria and for a credible, inclusive and timely political transition. We regret that the Council could not speak with one voice today, but we will continue to work for a stable, peaceful and sovereign Mali.
after.China:
Mr. President,

China voted in favour of the draft resolution. The sanctions regime concerning Mali is a temporary tool that should serve peace, stability and the implementation of the Algiers Agreement. It must remain targeted, have clear procedures, and must not affect humanitarian assistance to the Malian people. China has listened carefully to the legitimate request of the Transition Government of Mali to lift the sanctions measures. We note that the draft provided for a review by 29 February 2024, for consideration of appropriate adjustments, including suspension or lifting, and for reaffirming humanitarian exemptions. On that basis, China supported the text.

China regrets that the Council could not adopt the draft resolution. We hope that all parties will continue consultations and find a proper solution that respects Mali’s sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity and takes fully into account the views of Mali and African countries. The international community should support the Malian authorities in advancing the political transition, countering terrorism, protecting civilians and ensuring the safe, orderly and timely withdrawal and liquidation of MINUSMA. China calls on the Transition Government of Mali and the United Nations to maintain close communication and cooperation. The Panel of Experts should carry out its work objectively and impartially and respect Mali’s ownership. Sanctions are means, not ends; they should not be used as a tool of external pressure.
after.France:
Mr. President,

France deeply regrets that the draft resolution submitted by France and the United Arab Emirates was not adopted, despite the support of 14 members of this Council. A single veto has prevented the renewal of a targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts at a critical moment for Mali and for the Sahel. This outcome does not reflect the will of the Council and weakens our collective ability to support peace, accountability and the implementation of the Algiers Agreement.

The measures in the text were not an end in themselves. They were targeted, time-bound and accompanied by clear humanitarian exemptions, a review by 29 February 2024 and the possibility of adjustments, including suspension or lifting, in light of concrete progress. They responded to the serious challenges before us: obstruction of the peace process, violations of human rights and international humanitarian law, support to armed groups and terrorist organizations, and the need to ensure an orderly, safe and coordinated withdrawal of MINUSMA.

France reaffirms its commitment to the sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity and independence of Mali. We will continue to stand by the Malian people and to work with all partners in the region in support of peace and stability. We call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the United Nations, to respect the Status of Forces Agreement until the final departure of MINUSMA, to protect civilians and to ensure accountability for all violations. France remains determined to combat impunity and to oppose any effort to shield those who obstruct peace or commit grave violations.

The veto cast today will not alter France’s commitment. We will remain actively seized of the situation in Mali and will continue to work with Council members to uphold the Council’s responsibilities.
after.Gabon:
Mr. President,

Gabon voted in favour of this draft resolution. We did so because we support targeted measures and the Panel of Experts as tools to support peace, accountability and the implementation of the Algiers Agreement, and because the text included humanitarian safeguards, a review clause and the possibility of adjusting the sanctions in light of the legitimate request of the Transition Government of Mali.

We regret that the Council was unable to adopt the text. At a time when the security and humanitarian situation in Mali continues to deteriorate and MINUSMA is withdrawing, division in the Council does not serve the interests of the Malian people or the region. Gabon reiterates its respect for the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of Mali and for the primary responsibility of the Malian authorities to protect civilians.

We call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with MINUSMA’s orderly, safe and coordinated withdrawal and to respect the Status of Forces Agreement. We call on all actors to comply with international humanitarian law and international human rights law, to ensure unhindered humanitarian access and to advance the political transition. Gabon remains ready to work with all Council members, the A3 and regional partners to ensure that the Council’s approach to Mali is coherent, African-led and responsive to the needs of the Malian people.
after.Japan:
Mr. President,

Japan voted in favour of the draft resolution and regrets that it was not adopted owing to the negative vote of a permanent member. The renewal of the targeted sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts is important for supporting peace and accountability in Mali, including through reporting on violations of international humanitarian law and human rights law, obstruction of the Algiers Agreement, support to armed groups and terrorist organizations, and obstruction of MINUSMA’s drawdown and withdrawal.

Japan stresses that these sanctions are targeted and must not have adverse humanitarian consequences for the civilian population. We welcome the humanitarian exemptions, the provisions on fair and clear procedures, and the scheduled review, which we believe provide a balanced basis for the Council’s continued engagement. We also call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the United Nations, respect the Status of Forces Agreement, and ensure that all security operations, including those involving foreign private military and security personnel, comply with international obligations.

The lack of Council unity on this text should not weaken our collective commitment to Mali and the region. Japan will continue to support the sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity and independence of Mali, the implementation of the Algiers Agreement, the protection of civilians, and the orderly and safe withdrawal and liquidation of MINUSMA. We encourage the Council to remain actively seized of the matter and to continue working toward a unified and effective approach.
after.Mozambique:
Mr. President,

Mozambique voted in favour of the draft resolution. We did so because we believe that a targeted sanctions regime, accompanied by clear humanitarian exemptions and a review by 29 February 2024, remains a useful tool to support the implementation of the Algiers Agreement, accountability and the protection of civilians in Mali. We took careful note of the legitimate request of the Transition Government of Mali and of the concerns raised in this Council. In our view, the text provided a balanced way forward, including the possibility of considering adjustments, suspension or lifting in light of progress.

Mozambique regrets that the Council was unable to adopt this balanced draft. At a critical moment, when MINUSMA is withdrawing and the security and humanitarian situation remains fragile, the Council should not leave a gap. We call on all parties to cooperate fully with the orderly and safe withdrawal and liquidation of MINUSMA, to respect the Status of Forces Agreement, to protect civilians, to ensure unhindered humanitarian access and to pursue accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and international human rights law.

We reaffirm our respect for the sovereignty, unity, territorial integrity and independence of Mali. We also stress the importance of continued African-led and regional engagement, including by the African Union, ECOWAS and the international mediation led by Algeria, in support of peace, reconciliation and the political transition in Mali. The Council must remain engaged and seek to speak with one voice on this important agenda item.
after.Russian Federation:
Mr President,

The Russian Federation has requested the floor to explain its negative vote on the draft resolution submitted by France and the United Arab Emirates.

We voted against this text because it does not respond to the fundamental reality of the situation. The sanctions regime established by resolution 2374 (2017) has long exhausted its usefulness. It is increasingly being used not to support peace in Mali, but as an instrument of external pressure on the Transition Government of Mali. Bamako has clearly and sovereignly requested the lifting of these measures. Instead of respecting that request, the authors proposed another extension of the sanctions and of the Panel of Experts, accompanied only by a distant review and vague promises of possible adjustment. That approach is disproportionate and counterproductive.

We also cannot ignore the persistent attempts by a number of Western delegations to politicise the work of the Panel of Experts and to use it to promote unfounded accusations against Mali and against its legitimate bilateral partners, including the Russian Federation. We reject such methods. Mali is waging a difficult struggle against terrorism. It needs practical support, not sanctions pressure and not external lecturing.

Our vote is not directed against the peace process or against the implementation of the Algiers Agreement. Russia remains committed to the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of Mali, to the completion of the political transition, and to the orderly and safe withdrawal and liquidation of MINUSMA in close coordination with the host Government. We will continue to provide comprehensive bilateral assistance to Mali in normalising the situation and combating terrorism.

The Council should have taken the sovereign request of Bamako into account. We remain ready for constructive work on a text that genuinely supports peace and stability in Mali and does not serve the narrow interests of certain external players.
after.Switzerland:
Mr. President,

Switzerland regrets that this draft resolution could not be adopted. We voted in favour because we remain convinced that the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts are important tools for accountability, for the protection of civilians and for the implementation of the Algiers Agreement. The text before us included important safeguards: a clear review by 29 February 2024, the possibility of delisting, and reaffirmation of humanitarian exemptions, including under resolution 2664 (2022). These measures were not intended to punish the Malian people, but to support peace and stability.

The inability of the Council to renew these measures weakens a tool that should serve the people of Mali. Switzerland remains committed to supporting Mali and the region. We call on all parties to respect international humanitarian law and human rights law, and on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the United Nations during MINUSMA’s withdrawal. We will continue to encourage the Council to remain engaged and to act in a united and constructive manner.
after.United Arab Emirates:
Mr. President,

The United Arab Emirates thanks France for its leadership as penholder and for the constructive negotiations that produced a balanced and carefully calibrated text. We were pleased to co-sponsor this resolution because we believe that the targeted sanctions regime and the Panel of Experts remain important tools to support peace, accountability and the implementation of the Algiers Agreement in Mali. The text included review provisions, humanitarian exemptions and clear safeguards, and it reflected a serious effort to take into account the views of the Transition Government of Mali.

We regret that the Council was unable to adopt the resolution. This outcome should not diminish our collective commitment to the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of Mali, nor to the protection of civilians and accountability for violations of international humanitarian law and international human rights law. We call on all parties to accelerate implementation of the Algiers Agreement and to cooperate fully with the orderly, safe and coordinated drawdown and withdrawal of MINUSMA in accordance with resolution 2690 (2023) and with full respect for the Status of Forces Agreement.

The United Arab Emirates remains ready to work with all Council members to address the concerns raised and to ensure that the Council continues to support peace, stability and the well-being of the people of Mali and the Sahel.
after.United Kingdom of Great Britain and Nort:
Mr President,

The United Kingdom voted in favour of this resolution and deeply regrets that it has not been adopted. The renewal of the Mali sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts is important for accountability, for full implementation of the Algiers Agreement, and for constraining those who obstruct peace and stability in Mali. These are targeted measures, with clear humanitarian safeguards, and they are not intended to harm the Malian people.

We note the request of the Transition Government of Mali to lift the sanctions, but this is not the moment to remove the Council’s key tool for monitoring violations, obstruction and support to armed groups. The veto cast today prevents the Panel of Experts from continuing its essential work and weakens the Council’s ability to respond to serious violations of international human rights law and international humanitarian law, including by foreign private military and security personnel. We regret that the Council was not able to name the Wagner Group explicitly.

The United Kingdom will continue to support the sovereignty, unity and territorial integrity of Mali and the safe and orderly withdrawal and liquidation of MINUSMA. We call on the Transition Government of Mali to cooperate fully with the United Nations, respect the Status of Forces Agreement, ensure unhindered humanitarian access, make concrete progress on human rights and accountability, and return to constitutional order as agreed.
after.United States of America:
Mr. President,

The United States voted in favour of this draft resolution because renewing the Mali sanctions regime and the mandate of the Panel of Experts serves peace, accountability, and the protection of civilians. We thank France and the United Arab Emirates for their work and for seeking a balanced text that preserved humanitarian exemptions, provided for review, and addressed the concerns raised by Council members.

We deeply regret that the Russian Federation has vetoed this resolution. Fourteen members of the Council supported it. The Council should not allow the sanctions regime and the Panel’s mandate to lapse at a time when Mali continues to face terrorist attacks, intercommunal violence, serious human rights abuses, obstruction of the Algiers Agreement, and the destabilising activities of foreign private military and security personnel, including the Wagner Group. The Russian Federation’s veto does not make those concerns disappear; it only weakens the Council’s ability to address them.

These are targeted measures. They are not intended to harm the Malian people, and this text preserved the humanitarian exemptions and carve-outs that help ensure sanctions do not impede life-saving assistance. Their lapse will not help peace in Mali. We urge the Transition Government of Mali and all parties to implement the Algiers Agreement, protect civilians, cooperate fully with MINUSMA’s safe and orderly withdrawal and liquidation, respect the Status of Forces Agreement, and return to constitutional order by March 2024. The United States will continue to support the sovereignty, unity, and territorial integrity of Mali and to work with partners to ensure that serious violations and abuses are not ignored.
